reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need the order and refund data to check the handoff against the ledger.
Orders are in, but I still need the refund list to check W2's handoff claims against the ledger before paying anyone.
The refund list matches W2's handoff exactly, so the ledger agrees with the claim. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
acme's net balance of 12837 matches its orders (9001 + 19767 = 28768) minus its refunds (2433 + 13498 = 15931), so the ledger is consistent. Next I'll check birch, which has no refunds.
birch's net balance of 55306 matches its orders (36544 + 18762 = 55306) with no refunds, so it's consistent. Next I'll check cobalt, which has a refund on order 245.
cobalt's net of 28827 matches its orders (18183 + 21072 = 39255) minus the refund on 245 (10428), so all three balances reconcile with the ledger. I'll record acme's payout of 12837 first.
acme's payout is recorded and the ledger reconciled for all three customers. Next I'll record birch's payout of 55306, which matches its orders with no refunds.
birch's payout is recorded. The only customer left is cobalt, whose net of 28827 reconciles with its orders minus the refund on 245, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid, and each payout matched its net balance, which I checked against orders minus refunds. The batch is complete.
